hero.tagline: AI is <highlight>in the build</highlight>, not next to it.
hero.tagline_plain: AI is in the build, not next to it.
hero.subhead: I write production software with agents in the loop, ship developer tools at the model boundary, and bring teams that haven't gotten there yet across the line.

home.workBody: Not a productivity hack. The way the work gets built. Years of shipping production software end-to-end mean the AI-augmented work I do becomes product, not demos. I've led an engineering organization through AI tooling adoption end to end: evaluation, rollout, training, and the harder part of moving the engineers who weren't going to come along on their own. I build at the model boundary too, including production MCP tooling for the agents I work with day to day.
home.thinkTitle: From the system, not the pattern.
home.thinkBody: I reach for the underlying mechanism before I reach for prior art. When a system is unfamiliar, I'd rather study it from the foundations than copy a shape that worked somewhere else. On my own time I read papers and build cognitive architectures from scratch, partly because I want to understand the systems I'm shipping at a layer below the API. I bring the same discipline to my own code: every pull request on my main project gets reviewed against a written architectural document before it merges.

about.title: プロフィール。
about.body1: I'm a senior frontend engineer based in Charlotte, NC. I spent four years at Mediavine building their Journey product end-to-end with a small team (onboarding, an analytics engine, publisher dashboards) and led AI tooling adoption across the company. Before that: Tek Systems for React + GraphQL work, and Legal Associations Management, where I was promoted to team lead in nine months.
about.body2: For the past two years I've been building Sylphie, a cognitive architecture where the LLM is a voice box, not the decision-maker. I've shipped two MCP servers alongside the core system, and I review every pull request on the project against a written architectural constitution. It's a long bet that's taught me to design systems by reasoning about the problem rather than borrowing from prior art.
